subject: Request: Affirmation on model training & retention details for procurement
messages:
From: Alexa Moreno <alexa@streamlinehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@streamlinehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement question: do you ever use customer content to update models? + retention windows

Hi Naomi,

We're progressing through Streamline's procurement and security review. Two quick items we need clarified before we can finish the data-processing appendix:  

1) Does Redwood ever incorporate customer prompt/response content from the hosted API or Dedicated endpoints into model training, fine-tuning, or derivative model builds? If not, can you provide the exact language we can include in our SOW that captures the commitment?

2) For data retention: what are the retention windows for
   - request/response logs (plain-text prompts & completions),
   - debug snapshots/backups (DB snapshots, saved KV-cache dumps), and
   - operational telemetry (latency/cost traces tied to tokens) — are these retained longer than the request logs?

Also: are there any cases where ephemeral artifacts (KV caches, prefix caches) are persisted to long-term storage for debugging or crash-recovery beyond the stated request-log TTL? If yes, please outline the exception process.

Jordan (cc'd) may have some legal wording preferences. A one‑page statement we can attach to the contract would be ideal.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turn.

—Alexa
Director of Product, Streamline Health
[Attachment: SOW_template_Streamline_v3.docx]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alexa Moreno <alexa@streamlinehealth.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement question: do you ever use customer content to update models? + retention windows

Hi Alexa —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: we do not use customer-provided prompt/response content to update, fine-tune, or train our production model weights. We treat customer text from Hosted and Dedicated as in-scope for serving only, subject to the retention/export policies below. I'll include suggested contract language at the end.

Details and nuances:

- "No incorporation" commitment: Redwood's hosted API and Dedicated deployments do not feed customer prompts or completions into downstream model training or fine-tuning pipelines. This includes both automated training pipelines and manual experiments. The exception path is explicit opt-in research programs where a named customer signs a separate research agreement — these are rare and require written consent.

- Deployment modes and data separation: For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments where the customer manages the control plane, Redwood does not have access to customer request content unless customer explicitly enables support access. For Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Hosted, metadata and request/response logs are stored in our tenancy; Dedicated customers can opt for isolated storage buckets.

- Request/response logs TTL: default retention for text logs is 30 days for Hosted by default; Dedicated customers can configure retention down to 0 days (ephemeral) or request longer retention via contract. Logs are purged by a horizontal retention job; purge timelines may vary by shard but are auditable.

- Debug snapshots & backups: Snapshots (e.g., model-serving snapshots, debug session dumps, or infrastructure backups) are retained for a maximum of 90 days by default for Hosted environments. These snapshots deliberately exclude long-term archival of full-text customer prompts unless a customer request or an incident investigation requires it. Any snapshot that contains customer textual content is tagged and tracked in our change-log and removed per the retention schedule.

- Ephemeral artifacts (KV/prefix caches): KV caches and in-memory prefix caches are ephemeral by design. They are not written to durable, customer-visible long-term storage in normal operation. In the rare case of a crash that requires a persisted dump for forensic analysis, the dump is treated as a debug snapshot (see above) and follows the 90-day snapshot retention and special handling (restricted access, audit logging).

- Operational telemetry: telemetry (latency, error rates, token counts) is stored as aggregated metrics and traces. These do not contain raw prompt text and are retained separately (default 365 days for aggregations used in product analytics). Detailed traces that may reference request IDs are accessible in SRE/Support consoles for troubleshooting and are subject to RBAC and audit logs.

- Backups & archives: backups that power disaster recovery may contain derived metadata and truncated artifacts but do not contain full, searchable customer prompt/response stores. Long-term archives are not used to create training datasets.

- Exceptions and legal compulsion: if compelled by a valid legal process or in a security incident where access to text is strictly needed, Redwood follows the exception path: minimal-scope access, escalation to Legal + Security, customer notification where permitted, and a documented access log.

Suggested contract line (short form):
"Redwood Inference will not use Customer-provided text (prompts, uploaded documents, or generated completions) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve model weights or derivative models, unless Customer provides express written consent via a separate research or data-sharing agreement. Temporary artifacts required for debugging may be retained in accordance with the retention schedule in Annex A and will be accessible only to authorized personnel under audit logging."

Attachments: I've attached a one‑page factsheet that summarizes the retention windows and an editable SOW clause for procurement.

Next steps: Mina/Ben — can you confirm the SOW wording is OK for commercial and legal, and Mina, can we get a signed attestation template for Jordan if they request a signature?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy & Trust, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-data-residency-factsheet.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Alexa Moreno <alexa@streamlinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 13:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement question: do you ever use customer content to update models? + retention windows

Thanks Naomi — that language is great and concise. A couple of commercial notes for Streamline:

- We'll add Naomi's suggested sentence to the SOW under "Data Use" and include Annex A with the configurable retention windows.
- If Streamline needs a signed attestation, we can provide a one‑time attestation letter on corporate letterhead; Ben, can you draft a short attestation (1 paragraph) that matches the factsheet?

Alexa — we aim to have the SOW clause + attestation draft to you by end of day tomorrow (ET). If Jordan wants us to sign a separate attestation statement, we can do that but will route through Legal; it typically takes 2–3 business days.

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Director, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: draft-sow-clause-for-no-incorporation.docx]

From: Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@streamlinehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alexa Moreno <alexa@streamlinehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement question: do you ever use customer content to update models? + retention windows

Mina, Naomi — thanks for the quick and thorough response. Two small legal clarifications:  

1) Please confirm that the exception for "research programs" requires affirmative, narrow, documented opt-in from the customer (not just a checkbox buried in an account settings page).
2) For the snapshot exception used for crash forensic (the 90-day debug snapshot), can we get a brief bullet on who has access, how access is approved, and how the snapshot is destroyed? We need that for our SOC / vendor risk questionnaire.

If you can provide a one-paragraph signed attestation that covers the primary commitment (no incorporation for training) and a short bullet list answering (1) and (2), that will suffice for procurement.

Thanks — Jordan Reed
Senior Counsel, Streamline Health
